name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male figure noted for carrying out repairs beside his house, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:23. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not specified, his involvement in the rebuilding efforts highlights a role in the physical restoration of the community.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a recognition of God's assistance. This proper name, mentioned in Nehemiah 3:23, carries a theologically significant meaning typical of Hebrew names that express trust in God's providence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Maaseiah as Azariah's son, explicitly noted in Nehemiah 3:23. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded, limiting our understanding to this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's role in repairing the wall beside his house situates him within the collective effort to restore Jerusalem after exile, demonstrating faithful participation in God's work of rebuilding. Though additional historical details link him to significant leadership and spiritual lessons, the biblical record here emphasizes his contribution to the community's physical and spiritual restoration, underscoring the importance of obedience and service in God's plan.
